claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

Let me ask you the next question:

**Does Alex currently live with you in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, that's the thing - Alex does live with me, but we don't actually live in the UK. We're currently living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is an important detail as it affects eligibility.

**Which country are you currently living in? And are you or have you been a Crown servant (such as a diplomat or member of HM Forces)?**

This matters because you may still be able to get Child Benefit if you live in certain countries or if you're a Crown servant posted abroad.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: We're living in Spain at the moment. And no, I'm not a Crown servant - I'm not a diplomat or in the military or anything like that. We just moved abroad for work.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. This is helpful to understand your situation.

Since you're living in Spain and are not a Crown servant, I need to ask a few more questions to determine if you might still be eligible:

**Are you or have you been an EEA or Swiss national, or do you have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't have any of that. I'm just a regular UK citizen, but I don't have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Let me check one more thing:

**Are you paying UK National Insurance contributions while you're living in Spain, or do you have any other ongoing connection to the UK such as paying UK tax?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not paying UK National Insurance contributions while we're here in Spain. We moved here for work, so I'm working and paying taxes locally now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Eligibility Decision

Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex** at this time.

### The Reason:

While Alex is 8 years old (under 16) and lives with you - which would normally meet the basic eligibility requirements - the key issue is that **you and Alex are currently living in Spain, not in the UK**.

The fundamental rule for Child Benefit eligibility is that you must live in the UK. There are some exceptions to this rule, such as:
- Being a Crown servant (like a diplomat or member of HM Forces posted abroad)
- Living in certain specific countries under particular circumstances

However, since you're living in Spain for work purposes and are not a Crown servant, these exceptions don't apply to your situation.

### If Your Circumstances Change:

If you and Alex move back to the UK in the future, you would be able to claim Child Benefit at that time, as you would then meet the residency requirement.

I hope this information is helpful, even though it's not the outcome you were hoping for. Please feel free to ask if you have any other questions.
